title: Find the half of Earth that is land
hook: Earth is mostly water, but land bunches up. Can one half of the globe be mostly land?

knows: that Earth has more water than land
that the continents are unevenly spread
doesNotKnow: that even the landiest half of the Earth is more than half water

misconception: Somewhere there is a half of the Earth that is mostly land.
objective: The learner can say that the most land-heavy hemisphere, centred near Western Europe, is still just under half land, while the planet as a whole is about 29% land.

claims.text: The landiest half of the Earth on this map is centred near 42 N, 2 E, in Western Europe, and is about 47% land.
claims.source: Every hemisphere centre on a 2 degree grid, searched at build time over the lesson's own 2 degree land mask (mask.ts; cells cos-weighted): maximum 47.1% at 42 N, 2 E. The page recomputes the share at that centre from the same mask. Published land-hemisphere centres are near Nantes, France, at about 47 N, 2 W, with land about 47-49% (Boggs 1945; Wikipedia 'Land and water hemispheres'; from memory, not checked online). 1:110m omits small islands, so it is a slight underestimate; the lesson says 'on this map'.

claims.text: The whole planet is about 29% land.
claims.source: Cos-weighted share of land cells in the 2 degree mask: 29.0%. NOAA and USGS give about 29% (from memory, not checked online).

claims.text: The Northern Hemisphere is about 40% land.
claims.source: Same mask, hemisphere centred on the North Pole: 39.5% (shown rounded). The brief gives 39% by its own grid.

claims.text: The emptiest half, centred in the South Pacific near New Zealand, is only about 11% land.
claims.source: Minimum of the same build-time search: 10.9% at 42 S, 178 W, just east of New Zealand's North Island (place description from the coordinates).

recall.question: Someone says: 'From the right spot in space you could see a half of Earth that is mostly land.' Are they right?
options: No: even the landiest half is just under half land
Yes: the half centred on Asia is mostly land
Yes: the Northern Hemisphere is mostly land
recall.why: The most land you can fit in one hemisphere, centred near Western Europe, is still a little under half. The Northern Hemisphere is only about 40% land.
